plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap; check mutuality, cap quantum (fees paid/payable multiple), exclusion of indirect damages, and whether the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Section 1 carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Cross-check Section 20 indemnity to confirm it is not swept under the cap.

Section 20 should contain Vendor's third-party IP infringement and misconduct/data-breach indemnities; confirm defence obligation, remedy-or-replace path, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data content / unauthorised use only). Section 1 'Excluded Claims' and Sections 14-15 may cross-reference.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; if any restraint on Customer's business, competing products, or in-house build exists it would be buried in Customer Responsibilities, Access Rights/Licence restrictions, or General. Flag only if an actual restriction on our activities appears.

Scope (Sec 2), Order Forms/Affiliate Orders (Sec 4) and Customer Responsibilities (Sec 12) are the usual homes for sole-source or 'all requirements' language. Likely absent; confirm no preferred/exclusive supplier wording before marking missing.

Check Fees (Sec 7) and Order Forms (Sec 4) for any pricing-parity or best-terms clause. Direction rule: an MFN in our favour is fine and must not be flagged; only a clause obliging Customer to extend best terms to Vendor is a deviation.

A mutual or one-way non-solicit typically sits in General (Sec 30) or Customer Responsibilities (Sec 12). Test duration (12 months preferred), scope limited to personnel involved in the Services, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-application carve-out; one-way restraints on Customer only are the concern.

Section 9 governs termination rights; confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without early-termination fees or accelerated Fees, and that Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right mid-term. Check Sections 10 and 7 for any termination charge or non-refund mechanic.

Section 8 (Term and Renewal) is primary: test auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (30-60 days preferred, 90 days is the outer edge), and any renewal price uplift cap in Section 7 or the Order Form terms in Section 4.

Section 28 sets governing law, venue and any arbitration. Vendor is a Ltd., so watch for English/offshore law plus foreign-seated arbitration; accepted laws are NY, DE, CA or England and Wales with court jurisdiction. Note service-of-process interplay with Section 29.

Section 24 covers assignment and change of control. Confirm Customer may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger/asset sale without consent, and that Vendor cannot terminate or reprice on our change of control; check Section 9 for any linked termination trigger.

Section 14 should vest Deliverables in Customer and Section 15 confirm Customer owns Customer Data. Direction rule: flag any assignment of our IP or data to Vendor, broad feedback/derived-data or aggregate-data ownership grabs, and check the Sec 13 licence and Sec 1 definitions of Deliverable / Vendor Technology for overlap.

Section 13 is the grant. Test that use extends to Customer Affiliates and third-party contractors acting for Customer, that the licence is not revocable at will or unilaterally suspendable, and that any perpetual licence to Deliverables in Section 14 is consistent.

Section 22 is the Vendor's audit of our usage: check frequency (no more than annual), advance written notice, business-hours/remote-first conduct, confidentiality of auditors, and that Vendor bears cost absent a material shortfall. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may host the record-keeping obligation feeding the audit.

Direction rule: service credits flowing to us (likely in Sec 3 service levels) are welcome and must not be flagged. Look in Sections 7 and 9 for late-payment penalties beyond reasonable interest, early-termination or shortfall charges, or stipulated damages payable by Customer.

Section 19 should give a services/deliverables warranty of meaningful duration (90 days minimum) with re-performance plus refund as remedy; check for a broad disclaimer of implied warranties and whether Section 6 acceptance testing or Section 3 performance standards cut the warranty period short.

Section 18 exists; verify coverage lines and limits (commercial general liability, professional/E&O, cyber given Vendor hosts Customer Data per Sec 15/17), certificate delivery and notice of cancellation.

Check Order Forms (Sec 4) and Fees (Sec 7) for committed volumes, take-or-pay, non-reducible seat counts or no-downgrade-at-renewal language; if a commitment exists, confirm there is an exit or reduction right tied to Section 8/9 termination rights.

Section 11 is the transition/data-return clause; confirm a defined assistance period at agreed rates, export of Customer Data in a usable format, deletion certification, and that Section 10 does not permit Vendor to withhold data for disputed fees.
